mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues to stay near -40% and TRANSIT remains near -32%, retail and recreation will stay depressed because commuting-linked foot traffic is still weak; over the next four weeks RETAIL_REC should drift lower or remain below its last-four-week mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain within 5 points of their current depressed levels for the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A further pullback in RESIDENTIAL, paired with softer GROCERY_PHARM, indicates more out-of-home substitution into essential errands but not discretionary shopping; this should shave retail leisure visits within two weeks and push RETAIL_REC down.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 8% while GROCERY_PHARM stays below -10%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 2 weeks after RESIDENTIAL drops below 8% and GROCERY_PHARM remains below -10%.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS from negative territory back above zero signals better outdoor weather and stronger weekend activity, which can spill into nearby shopping trips and lift retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from negative to positive week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 4 weeks even though PARKS turns positive and stays positive for at least 2 consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT stops improving and WORKPLACES also fail to recover, households face fewer routine city-center visits, so discretionary retail traffic should soften within one week and remain weaker over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT declines week-on-week while WORKPLACES is still below -35%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within 1 week despite a week-on-week TRANSIT decline and WORKPLACES staying below -35%.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently low GROCERY_PHARM suggests consumers are still limiting nonessential trips and bundling errands outside shopping districts; that pattern typically precedes weaker retail visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week average while GROCERY_PHARM stays at or below -10% for the full next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL continues edging up while TRANSIT stays subdued, people are substituting home-based time for shopping trips; that combination should reduce retail-and-recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 9% and TRANSIT stays below -30%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 2 weeks after RESIDENTIAL exceeds 9% while TRANSIT remains below -30%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in PARKS together with a concurrent rise in TRANSIT reflects stronger movement intensity across leisure and access modes, which should lift retail-and-recreation mobility over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over the next 4 weeks even though PARKS and TRANSIT both trend upward for at least 2 consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Under a restrictive regime, an additional drop in WORKPLACES below its current level tightens the commute-to-shopping channel and depresses discretionary retail visits quickly; the effect should appear within one week and be visible over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays above its prior 4-week mean after WORKPLACES falls below -40%.
